records.question: In E28 blue recovery, what did opposing-end grasps enable, and what did fresh localization, face-to-grasp height and endpoint feedback distinguish from orientation alone?
records.text:
IF a left opposing-end grasp exposes the aperture and retains blue after lift/transport, E28 supplies a combined candidate: inspect current aperture/peg relation and noncollinear face height, correct the measured relation, use staged entry, then open and withdraw vertically. The first recovery, shallow third pickup and final left regrasp supported this chain; clear-hand peg/aperture persistence and layer-consistent face heights supported the results.
This is not an orientation-only success rule. Early widthwise entry changed bar-to-jaw presentation. Free-space leveling restored agreeing face samples, but renewed entry still lacked visible passage and had a large measured endpoint residual despite complete execution. Lift-away retained blue. A later opposing-end pickup also missed its descent endpoint yet retained on lift.
Fresh tip/aperture picks distinguished XY registration from face level; earlier selected peg surfaces were not interchangeable with tip localization. The shallow third capture put the face below the grasp point, unlike the above-grasp face in the first/final captures. Historical hand height therefore did not specify object height. Fresh tabletop aperture picks also differed from the prior hand target, without establishing object displacement.
Planner rejections executed no actions, unlike witnessed entry nonarrival and actual releases. Grasp, localization, pickup depth, attitude, piece/layer and release setup changed together.

Tilt/drift, loss of peg-aperture persistence after opening/clearance, or inconsistent unloaded height disconfirms the corresponding positive response. Distinguish level, XY registration, signed face height, measured tracking and released outcome; neither command completion nor aperture color substitutes for these checks. Separate zero-action planner rejection from executed physical response.

events.answer:
The failures do not establish one common cause.
• Largest-left: retained at staging, but one finger displaced about 2 mm during carry without a new opening request. Arrival was 4.3 mm above its measured closing height. Shift/tilt or incomplete support remain plausible; side-lying was confirmed only after the following withdrawal/exchange (e000660), not isolated to opening.
• Second-smallest-right: sampled jaw seating persisted through lift/carry; arrival was 1.7 mm above closure. It became side-lying during the 0.16 s opening-only interval with essentially stationary EEF (e001932→e001951). Withdrawal was therefore not required for this failure; opening impulse versus unsupported settling remains unresolved.
• Middle/smallest-left: arrival heights were within about 0.2/0.5 mm of closure, and both stood after opening and clearance. This is a positive placement contrast, not proof of a height threshold or that diagonal transport inevitably fails.
Recovery: the fallen largest's right head grasp retained a vertical lift and subsequent reorientation to an approximately upright configuration, but it was side-lying again by e001784. Retained reorientation is demonstrated; durable upright placement is not.
For the next recovery, distinguish doll-to-pad attitude and base support from EEF height, then assess persistence after opening and clearance. Neither simply lowering farther nor slowing opening is a demonstrated cure. A visible/measured base-to-table gap and doll attitude immediately before opening, plus settling observed before withdrawal, could distinguish the remaining explanations.

arguments.note: The largest has remained seated in the closed grip through the preceding execution; open it now and check persistence before withdrawing. Lift the newly enclosed second-smallest into the left workspace for its upright recovery.

The second-smallest now appears seated at the row, and its jaw seating changed during the final lowering rather than remaining suspended at the earlier height. Open in place and inspect whether it stands before withdrawing.
The second-smallest stands after opening. Withdraw vertically without changing wrist orientation, then verify all five dolls and the row before returning the left arm home.

records.text: Correction of the same first yellow square, starting from e000682. Regrasp/closing receipt e000734 executed all 14 selected actions; e000735 shows the square between the pads. Lift request e000753 executed all 3 actions; e000754 shows the hole clear of the peg while the square remains between the pads. Combined lateral/downward request e000773 executed all 4 actions; e000774 shows a tilted square with peg visible inside the hole. Opening receipt e000789 executed all 3 actions; e000790 shows the square visibly lower with substantial peg protrusion. Withdrawal receipt e000826 executed all 9 actions; e000827 shows the square still down around the protruding peg after the pads clear. This is a visual response contrast, not evidence that a particular offset, release or hypothesized pad constraint caused success. The read sources do not establish a numerical corrected post-withdrawal top height, descent magnitude, contact state or repeatability.

events.answer:
Both recoveries provide positive but scoped evidence for empty closed-pad face pressing followed by unloaded review. Third blue changed from sampled unloaded heights of 0.815032–0.839387 m to 0.814022–0.814196 m after two downward increments and clearance. First star changed from 0.810119–0.823950 m to 0.788199–0.788209 m. Clear-hand RGB showed peg passage and substantially flatter, lower faces in both cases.
Tracking differed: blue's two presses ended about 1.84 and 1.67 mm above their requested heights; star's first ended 1.55 mm above, while its second ended 4.69 mm above with 3.08 mm lateral residual, despite complete execution. These are measured EEF responses, not force measurements or object displacements.
Prior held star correction reduced sampled face-height spread from about 12.0 to 0.63 mm, yet entry, opening and clearance still left it tilted. The later recovery therefore cannot be credited to held leveling alone. The two press sequences are changed-condition observations, not replication, a universal pressing rule or a demonstrated preference over regrasp. Contact mechanism, individual contributions, repeatability, safe force limits and hidden seating remain unknown; simulator depth precision is not a real-world tolerance.

records.text: E27 final-yellow later response during empty-hand recovery approach, e002292/e002383/e002384. Before RGB and inspection e002295 show an ungrasped tilted square, with face/rim heights spanning 0.815719–0.838990 m. The recovery-approach request changed hand position and pitch/roll but requested no closure; 27/27 actions executed. Measured grasp Z rose 40.64 mm, wrist orientation changed 49.97 degrees and the fingers remained open. At the post endpoint the jaws are empty, the peg is visible in the square's opening and the square appears level. Same-post inspection e002387 gives left/right/far/near heights 0.814098/0.814083/0.814078/0.814110 m. The level unloaded state was observed before any new closure, not after a verified regrasp or press. Endpoint evidence bounds the change to this interval but cannot separate elapsed dynamics, clearance or incidental contact, nor certify a contact-free path, hidden seating contacts or a corrective mechanism.
